title: Value, Scope And Pilot Decisions Checkpoint

questions.prompt: 120 tickets/day × 60% eligible × 5 minutes saved × 20 days × 50% adoption gives what modeled monthly capacity?

options.label: 60 hours before review, training and operating overhead.

questions.explanation: The arithmetic is 120×0.6×5×20×0.5/60 = 60 hours. It is modeled capacity, not a measured result or automatic expenditure reduction.

questions.prompt: A pilot team reports 400 model calls as its success metric. What is missing?

options.label: A baseline and user outcome with a denominator, window and countermetric.
A larger number of model calls so the result looks significant.
A screenshot of the infrastructure dashboard instead of task evidence.

questions.explanation: Activity does not establish value. Define task success and harmful side effects against a comparable baseline; volume and screenshots cannot replace that contract.

questions.prompt: Refund automation is added to a two-week read-only pilot. How should the FDE respond?

options.label: Accept it while silently removing permission checks.
Reject all discussion without explaining the consequence.
Offer explicit scope/date options and obtain a decision from the responsible owner.

questions.explanation: The new action changes risk and delivery work. Options preserve a shared outcome while making tradeoffs visible; hidden quality cuts and unexplained refusal do not.

questions.prompt: A pilot has features and a deadline but no decision owner or stop criteria. What should be added?

options.label: A commitment to expand before the pilot has produced evidence.
Who decides continuation, using which evidence and failure thresholds.
A rule to continue indefinitely if any user likes the demo.

questions.explanation: A pilot must inform a decision. Undefined continuation or precommitted expansion removes the learning function and can turn a trial into unsupported production.
